docs.title: About
docs.text: Pixelette Holdings brings together venture partnership capabilities and specialist businesses supporting technology development, market growth and organisational readiness.

docs.title: Practical support
docs.text: Hands-on expertise across engineering, commercial development and enterprise readiness.

docs.title: Aligned interests
docs.text: Commercial arrangements designed to align contributions, responsibilities and longer-term interests.

docs.title: Disciplined delivery
docs.text: Clearly defined scope, agreed milestones and measurable delivery progress.

docs.title: Real-world impact
docs.text: Supporting ventures developing products and services with practical commercial applications.

docs.title: The Pixelette Group
docs.text: Four businesses with distinct responsibilities, working independently or together according to the needs of each venture or client.

docs.title: How we work together
docs.text: Each business brings its own expertise to an engagement. Pixelette Holdings coordinates selected venture partnerships, with the relevant group businesses contributing services according to the agreed requirements.

docs.title: Quality and information security
docs.text: Pixelette Technologies holds ISO 9001 and ISO/IEC 27001 certifications for quality and information security management.

docs.title: What is Pixelette Holdings?
docs.text: Pixelette Holdings brings together venture partnership capabilities and specialist businesses supporting technology development, market growth and organisational readiness.

docs.title: What does each group business do?
docs.text: Pixelette Holdings develops selected venture partnerships through Hybrid Sweat Equity. Pixelette Technologies designs and builds digital products. Pixelette Marketing supports brand and commercial growth. Pixelette Certified supports compliance readiness and preparation for independent assessment.

docs.title: Accessibility Statement
docs.text: Pixelette Holdings aims to meet WCAG 2.2 level AA. Accessibility is treated as a build requirement, not a retrofit.

docs.title: Explore a partnership
docs.text: Tell us about your venture. Share a few details and Pixelette Holdings will review your enquiry. It does not create a partnership or an investment commitment, and it does not promise a reply by a set date.

docs.title: What to send
docs.text: Your name, a email, the venture, its stage and a short description. You do not need a pitch deck or a cap table at this point.

docs.title: How it is used
docs.text: If you send the enquiry, Pixelette Holdings Ltd uses it to decide whether a conversation is relevant and to reply. The privacy notice describes that handling.

docs.title: What happens afterwards
docs.text: A person may review an enquiry that has actually been received. There is no promised response time. A reply does not create a partnership or commitment.

docs.title: What it does not do
docs.text: It does not create a partnership, a delivery obligation, an investment, or a commitment by either side. Any commercial terms would be a separate agreement.

docs.title: What this enquiry is for
docs.text: A conversation about delivery and a possible Hybrid Sweat Equity arrangement. It is not a request for Pixelette to invest cash, and there is no standard paid pilot on this page.

docs.title: How do I explore a partnership with Pixelette Holdings?
docs.text: Tell us about your venture on the apply page. Submitting an enquiry does not create a partnership or an investment commitment, and it does not promise a reply by a set date.

docs.title: Enquiry
docs.text: This page is not a receipt. An email you send yourself is the message that can be received.

docs.title: Contact
docs.text: Contact Pixelette Holdings about a general enquiry, a strategic partnership, an incubator or accelerator programme, or a capital relationship. Founders should explore a partnership.

docs.title: Write to us
docs.text: Use the form for general, strategic, incubator or capital enquiries. Your answers are stored so we can reply, and the team is notified by email when that is configured. Founders should explore a partnership instead.

docs.title: Hybrid Sweat Equity
docs.text: How Hybrid Sweat Equity works: agreed professional services in exchange for cash fees and equity participation, with the detailed terms set out in each venture’s agreements.

docs.title: Agreed cash contribution
docs.text: The founder and Pixelette agree what portion of the professional fee is paid in cash, and when. There is no published standard split.

docs.title: Professional services
docs.text: Pixelette provides the delivery described in the agreed scope. The work is contracted. Customers, revenue and fundraising are not.

docs.title: Equity participation
docs.text: Any equity is set out in the commercial and shareholder agreements. It is not a fixed allocation, and it is not presented here as a standard percentage.

docs.title: Milestones
docs.text: Responsibilities can be linked to milestones defined in the agreements. What counts as acceptance is agreed for that venture, not assumed from this page.

docs.title: How the partnership works
docs.text: Cash, delivery, equity and milestones are agreed for the venture. The precise commercial model depends on its circumstances.

docs.title: From concept to launch
docs.text: Five stages, used to organise the work. They are not guaranteed completion times.

docs.title: Protecting the partnership
docs.text: Every venture is different. We establish clear commercial, delivery and governance arrangements through agreements tailored to the partnership.

docs.title: Explore a partnership
docs.text: Tell us about the venture. An enquiry does not create a partnership, and it does not promise a reply within a set time.

docs.title: Is Hybrid Sweat Equity free development?
docs.text: No. Pixelette contributes agreed professional services in exchange for a combination of cash fees and equity participation. It is not free work, and it is not a cash investment by Pixelette.

docs.title: Is there a standard equity percentage?
docs.text: No. The allocation of equity, milestone conditions, founder rights and governance arrangements are established in the relevant agreements. A percentage on this website would be misleading.

docs.title: Do founders keep complete control?
docs.text: Decision-making rights depend on the shareholder and governance documents for that venture. This page does not promise that every founder retains complete control.

docs.title: Is a paid pilot required before a conversation?
docs.text: No standard paid pilot, validation retainer or other preliminary fee is required by this website. If any preliminary work is contracted, that is a separate agreement.

docs.title: Does following the stages guarantee a launch, customers or investment?
docs.text: No. The stages describe how delivery can be organised. They are not a timetable, and they are not a promise of customers, revenue or external investment.

docs.title: What should I do if I want to discuss a partnership?
docs.text: Explore a partnership. You can start on the startups page first if you want a clearer next step. Submitting an enquiry does not create a partnership.

docs.title: Building a technology startup: what founders should validate before development begins
docs.text: What a technology startup should test before engineering starts: the problem, the customer, the commercial assumption, MVP scope and the resources the work will actually take.

docs.title: Founder control and equity dilution: what to consider before signing
docs.text: Economic ownership and decision-making rights are different. What to read in voting, reserved matters, vesting and exit clauses before signing a shareholder arrangement.

docs.title: From MVP to investment readiness: building evidence that matters
docs.text: Why a working product, user evidence, commercial validation and investment preparation are different stages, and why none of them guarantees external investment.

docs.title: Insights
docs.text: Explore practical perspectives on venture formation, equity partnerships, founder governance and the decisions involved in developing and growing technology businesses.

docs.title: Services for equity: how startup partnerships can be structured
docs.text: How a services-for-equity partnership can combine cash and shares, and why ownership, milestones and governance have to be written down for that venture.
